correctness.rationale: The precise cyclic read-distance condition is equivalent to requiring that every open neighborhood of an edge graph be separated by three cyclic positions. This gives degree at most \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\). When \(n=3m\), any maximum-degree neighborhood is an entire residue class, and maximum-degree vertices in all three classes would force a fixed-point-free involution on three labels. The strict edge bound follows. Explicit circulant, antipodal and matching constructions attain the general degree bound in the other residues; \(K_{m,m}\sqcup K_m\) attains the strict bound. Every length \(n\ge6\) is covered; independent finite read-metric checks reproduce the conclusions.

originality.rationale: The 2016 primary b-read and linear MDS papers address unconstrained or linear code classes; their size bounds do not yield the binary all-weight-two optimum. De Alba et al. prove the ordinary-cycle two-token independence number but not the square-cycle case. The 2025 bounds normalize constant b-symbol weight, not Hamming weight. Direct statement/implication comparisons and alias searches do not reveal equivalent published coverage. Residual risk: an unindexed result under graph-theoretic names.

value.rationale: A natural constant-Hamming-weight restriction yields a sharp, complete all-length three-symbol read capacity. The modulo-three failure of the naive degree bound is structural and mathematically motivated by cycle-square packing; constructive optimality includes odd-parity lengths. This exact optimal-capacity statement is not implied by general linear MDS construction or constant b-weight inequalities, and it provides definite limits for sparse three-read marker codes.
